note: Joining positions 2 and 3 with one word for the way across, "the crossing": position 3 alone, the crossing on a position-neck with cross and both crossing notes ringed, then positions 1 to 3 framed on one neck, in turn and then without stopping. Moves holds any key and 70 to 90 bpm, so the title and text name them as params, and the last line says what stays the same in another key.

exercise.title: {{=key}} minor pentatonic: join positions 2 and 3
exercise.why: Position 3 starts on the notes where position 2 ends, so one slide along the G string carries a phrase from the second into the third.

cells.text:
Under this text is the neck with position 3 of the {{=key}} minor pentatonic scale: each dot is a note to play, and the ringed dots are the {{1}} notes. Start on the lowest dot on the low E string, play both dots on each string up to the high e string, then come back down the same way, at your own pace.
It is the widest of the five positions, so let your hand open for the notes on the G and B strings.
Practice until you can start it from any ringed {{1}}.

The neck below shows only the crossing: position 2 of the {{=key}} minor pentatonic scale on the low strings, position 3 on the high strings. Climb position 2 from the low E string. On the G string, slide from the ringed {{5}} up to the ringed {{b7}} and finish the climb in position 3.
Come back down the same way, sliding from {{b7}} down to {{5}}.
If the slide lands on the wrong fret, slow your hand down and let your ear tell you when the note matches the dot.

Press Play below to start the metronome at {{=bpm}}. The neck under it frames positions 1, 2 and 3. Play position 1 from the low E string up to the high e string and back down, one note per beat, then position 2, then position 3.
When each one feels steady, play all three without stopping, crossing on the G string each time.
{{?key}}In another key the three positions sit on other frets, and the crossing is still the slide from {{5}} to {{b7}} on the G string.
